queue.title: Powered width-1 vs width-2 proposal replication
Adaptive proposal-allocation swarm
queue.hypothesis: The width-2 benefit is concentrated in resampling particular epistemic designer families. Allocating the second proposal-generation budget to the highest-value designer subsets can retain or improve width-2 recovery while using less compute than uniformly duplicating all five designers.
queue.design: Instrument proposal source identity. Compare baseline five-designer set plus one independently resampled proposal from INFOGAIN, FALSIFY, CHEAPEST, RIVAL, or WEAKTIE, and selected low-cost subsets. Use shallow one-step scoring, RNG-isolated observations, equal intervention budget, and compute accounting. Screen on matched worlds, then power the best allocation against uniform width-2.
queue.primary_metric: Pareto performance over edge error and compute time

established_findings: Unconditional two-step search does not improve the primary metric after RNG isolation and costs roughly 9x compute.
Initial-state and local-margin depth gates failed to justify deeper search.
Moderate proposal breadth (two independent five-designer root sets) improves edge recovery over width-1 at n=48, with paired CI excluding zero, and raises exact MAP recovery at roughly 2x compute.
dynamic_enqueue_rules: Every completed experiment must generate at least one next candidate unless a stronger queued candidate already tests the same uncertainty.
Falsification never empties the queue; it narrows or redirects it.
Do not enqueue equivalent retries without a changed causal hypothesis, state representation, reward, search depth, world model, or evaluation design.
Promote surprising anomalies and control victories into diagnostic experiments.
Maintain matched resource budgets and preserve all negative results.
